input.sha256_scope: The committed classic-v1-benchmark-page/input.png, which four of the eight cases use at 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees. The other four are deterministic synthetic pages generated by formula on both sides.
input.provenance: No new input pixels. Four cases reuse an already-committed fixture PNG and its rotations; the other four are generated by a trivial closed-form expression reproduced identically in the capture tool and the Rust test.

limitations: Preprocessing is transcribed from the C++ deployment source and the artifact's inference.yml, not imported: there is no Python predictor for this model. An upstream change to either would not be detected here.
Only the 90-degree rotations of one page are exercised. Real skew, arbitrary angles, and pages whose content is not text are untested.
The model outputs are recorded rather than reproduced offline. The committed fixture checks that this port builds the same input tensor; running the real model needs the provisioned artifact.
No rotation is applied by this fixture. Deciding an angle and acting on it are separate, and the inverse geometry that acting on it requires is not implemented.
